CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Mayor  www.SanMarinoCA.gov
Tony Chou, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Hunter Chang, Council Member  City Hall Council Chamber

John Chou, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive
Calvin Lo, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  FRIDAY, JULY 25, 2025 AT 8:30 AM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned meetings are held on the last Friday of every month at 8:30 a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov or by phone at (626)
300-0705 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City
will do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.SanMarinoCA.gov/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:

  Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@SanMarinoCA.gov until 3:00
  p.m. the day before the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will
  be distributed to City Council during the meeting. Any comments received after 3:00

AGENDA – JULY 25, 2025  PAGE 1 of 6
   p.m. will be included in the public comment record but not provided to City Council at
  the meeting.
  Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference
  module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted after the in-
  person comments. Written Zoom comments will be read or summarized, then printed
  and made part of the public record for the meeting.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chang, Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Vice Mayor Chou, and
Mayor Shepherd Romey

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 24 hours prior to each special meeting at the following locations: City
Hall, 2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the
Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.SanMarinoCA.gov.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to place
limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

 1.  PUBLIC HEARING TO CONSIDER ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. O-25-
  1418 AMENDING THE FOLLOWING MUNICIPAL CODE SECTIONS: (1)
  23.13.04 (B)(2)(D) TO INCREASE THE MAXIMUM HEIGHT FOR HEDGES
  IN THE FRONT YARD WITHIN THE R-1 ZONE, AREA DISTRICT II TO
  FIVE FEET- SIX INCHES (5’-6”); (2) 25.01.02 (D) TO PROHIBIT
  CONSTRUCTION ON MARTIN LUTHER KING JR. DAY; AND (3) 23.06.11
  TO INCLUDE CALAMITIES AS DETERMINED BY THE COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council conduct a public hearing,
  determine whether to amend the code regarding hedge heights as drafted by staff or
  as recommended by the Planning Commission, and introduce for first reading

AGENDA – JULY 25, 2025  PAGE 2 of 6
   Ordinance No. O-25-1418. If the City Council agrees, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to waive full reading and introduce by title only Ordinance No. O-25- 1418, an
  Ordinance of the San Marino City Council amending Municipal Code Sections (1)
  23.13.04 (B)(2)(D) to increase the maximum height for hedges in the front yard within
  the R-1 zone, Area District II to five feet- six inches (5’-6”); (2) 25.01.02 (D) to prohibit
  construction on Martin Luther King Jr. Day; and (3) 23.06.11 to include calamities as
  determined by the community development director.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  APPOINTMENT OF MEMBERS TO CITY OF SAN MARINO LIBRARY
  BOARD OF TRUSTEES ADVISORY BODY

  Recommendation: The Council Liaisons for the Library Board of Trustees recommend
  the Council appointment of two (2) regular members, each commencing on July 10,
  2025. If Council concurs, the appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to appoint Sandy Wu and Diana Nixon as regular members of the Library
  Board of Trustees to serve terms ending May 31, 2028, and to appoint Jody Nichols as
  an alternate member to serve a partial term ending on May 31, 2026.”

3.  FIND THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDED
  FY 2024-25 ADA SIDEWALK CURB RAMP PROJECT EXEMPT UNDER THE
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA), APPROVE THE
  PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS AVAILABLE AT THE OFFICE OF THE CITY
  CLERK AND AT THE DIAS, AWARD A CONSTRUCTION AGREEMENT TO
  CT&T CONCRETE PAVING IN THE LOW BASE BID AMOUNT OF
  $159,379.19, AND REJECT ALL OTHER BIDS; AND AUTHORIZE THE
  PARKS AND PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR/CITY ENGINEER TO APPROVE
  CONTINGENCIES IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $15,938

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council 1) find the project categorically
  exempt under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Sections
  15301(c) and 15302 of Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations (Class
  1, Existing Facilities exemption), 2) approve the Plans and Specifications available at
  the office of the City Clerk and at the dais, 3) award a Construction Agreement to CT&T
  Concrete Paving Company, and 4) authorize the Parks and Public Works Director/City
  Engineer to approve contract change orders and other contingencies in an amount not
  to exceed $15,938. If the Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion would be:

  “I move to 1) find the ADA Sidewalk Curb Ramp Project exempt from review under the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Sections 15301(c) and 15302
  of Title 14, Chapter 3 of the California Code of Regulations (Class 1, Existing Facilities
  exemption), 2) approve the Plans and Specifications available at the office of the City
  Clerk and at the dais, 3) award a Construction Agreement to CT&T Concrete Paving
  Company, Inc. for the CDBG-funded ADA Sidewalk Curb Ramp Project No. 24/25-
  9272A in the amount of $159,379.19, reject all other bids, and authorize the City

AGENDA – JULY 25, 2025  PAGE 3 of 6
   Manager to execute the Agreement, 5) authorize the Parks and Public Works
  Director/City Engineer to approve contract change orders in an amount not to exceed
  $15,938, and 6) Approve the FY 2025-26 budget adjustment needed.

4.  APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT NO. 2 WITH RINCON CONSULTANTS, INC.
  TO PROVIDE CONTRACT PLANNING SERVICES THROUGH SEPTEMBER
  14, 2028

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve Amendment No. 2,
  direct the City Attorney to prepare the amendment, and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the amendment. If Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, the
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve Amendment No. 2 in the not to exceed amount of $100,000 with
  Rincon Consultants, Inc., for Planning consulting services, direct the City Attorney to
  prepare Amendment No. 2 consistent with the scope outlined in the staff report, and
  authorize the City Manager to execute said amendment.”

5.  AWARD OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH WILLDAN
  FINANCIAL SERVICES FOR A DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE STUDY

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the contract and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the contract with Willdan Financial Services, approve the necessary
  budget adjustments, and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement.”

6.  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE RETIREMENT HEALTHCARE PROGRAM
  ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES AND RECORDKEEPING AGREEMENT
  BETWEEN TEACHERS INSURANCE AND ANNUITY ASSOCIATION OF
  AMERICA (TIAA) AND THE CITY OF SAN MARINO DATED MAY 1, 2017,
  APPROVING THE ANNUAL FEE FOR TRUST SERVICES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council to approve Amendment No. 1 to
  the Retirement Healthcare Program Administrative Services and Recordkeeping
  Agreement between Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America (TIAA)
  and the City of San Marino dated May 1, 2017, approving the annual fee for trust
  services and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement. If the City Council
  concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve Amendment No. 1 to the Retirement Healthcare Program
  Administrative Services and Recordkeeping Agreement between Teachers Insurance
  and Annuity Association of America (TIAA) and the City of San Marino dated May 1,
  2017, and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement.”

7.  ACCEPTANCE OF CANNABIS TAX FUND GRANT PROGRAM (CTFGP)
  FUNDING IN THE AMOUNT OF $255,041.13 AND ADOPTION OF
  RESOLUTION R-25-22

AGENDA – JULY 25, 2025  PAGE 4 of 6
   Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council approve the agreement for
  the Cannabis Tax Fund Grant Funding and authorize the City Manager or his designee
  to execute any and all agreements and documents necessary to accept and expend
  the grant funds in an amount not to exceed $255,041.13 in the fiscal year ending June
  30, 2026. Staff also recommends the approval of Resolution No. R-25-22. If the City
  Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve and authorize the Chief of Police and the City Manager or their
  designee to enter into the agreement with the California Highway Patrol in an amount
  not to exceed $255,041.13, approve budget adjustments needed, and adopt
  Resolution No. R-25-22.”

8.  ACCEPTANCE OF A $150,000 DONATION FROM THE HUNTINGTON
  LIBRARY, ART MUSEUM, AND BOTANICAL GARDENS FOR RECEIPT IN
  THE CAPITAL PROJECTS FUND

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council accept the donation and approve
  budget adjustments needed. If the Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to accept the donation of $150,000 from the Huntington Library, Art Museum,
  and Botanical Gardens; authorize the Finance Department to record the receipt of the
  donation in the Capital Projects Fund; and amend the FY 2025-26 revenue budget to
  recognize revenue of $150,000 in the Capital Projects Fund (Account #394-00-3601-
  0000).”

9.  CONSIDERATION OF RESOLUTION NO. R-25-16 AMENDING JOB
  CLASSIFICATIONS

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council adopt Resolution No. R-25-16
  amending job classifications. If the Council agrees with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to adopt Resolution No. R-25-16 amending job classifications.”

10. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF JUNE 2025

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of June
  2025.”

11. RECEIVE AND FILE MONTHLY DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR JUNE
  2025

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of June 2025. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

AGENDA – JULY 25, 2025  PAGE 5 of 6
   “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of June
  2025.”

 12. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the June 2025 Minutes. If
  the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be:

  “I move to approve the Minutes of the Regular Meeting of June 11, 2025, and the
  Adjourned Regular Meeting of June 27, 2025.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

Posted: 07/18/2025  ALISON WALKER
  CITY CLERK

AGENDA – JULY 25, 2025  PAGE 6 of 6
